Write f=[a,b,c]. Two integral binary quadratic forms f and g are equivalent if there is a matrix
U=(αγ​βδ​)∈SL2​(Z)
(1)
such that
g(x,y)=f(αx+βy,γx+δy).
(2)
Equivalently, the group SL2​(Z) acts on forms by integral unimodular changes of variables.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

b

Words: 94 Articles: 1
1G OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 94
b OurBigBook.com
Suppose g=[A,B,C] is obtained from f=[a,b,c] by such a change of variables. Expanding shows that each of A,B,C is an integer linear combination of a,b,c. Therefore every common divisor of a,b,c divides A,B,C.
The inverse of a matrix in SL2​(Z) again has integral entries and determinant one. Applying the same argument to U−1 shows that every common divisor of A,B,C divides a,b,c. The two coefficient triples consequently have the same greatest common divisor, up to sign, so one form is primitive exactly when the other is.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

∣b∣≤a≤c,
(3)
with b≥0 when equality occurs in either inequality. Its discriminant is
b2−4ac=−80.
(4)

ac=20+4b2​.
(5)
Checking the finitely many possibilities with ∣b∣≤a≤c gives
[1,0,20],[3,2,7],[3,−2,7],[4,0,5].
(6)

2I OurBigBook.com
Runge's polynomial approximation theorem says that if K⊂C is compact, C∖K is connected, and f is holomorphic on a neighborhood of K, then for every ε>0 there is a polynomial p such that
supK​∣p−f∣<ε.
(8)
Let
S={z:∣z∣=1, Rez≤0}.
(9)
This arc is compact, its complement is connected, and 1/z is holomorphic on a neighborhood of it. Applying Runge with error 1/n gives a polynomial qn​ satisfying
supz∈S​∣qn​(z)−z−1∣<n1​,
(10)
which is the requested uniform approximation.
For the pointwise construction, for n≥2 set
Kn+​Kn−​Kn0​​={z:∣z∣≤1−1/n, Rez≥1/n},={z:∣z∣≤1−1/n, Rez≤−1/n},={iy:∣y∣≤1−1/n},Kn​=Kn+​∪Kn−​∪Kn0​.​
(11)
The three pieces are disjoint compact sets and C∖Kn​ is connected. Define a function on a neighborhood of Kn​ to equal 1, −1, and 0 on neighborhoods of Kn+​, Kn−​, and Kn0​, respectively. It is holomorphic because those neighborhoods may be chosen disjoint. Runge supplies a polynomial Pn​ such that
∣Pn​−1∣<1/n on Kn+​,∣Pn​+1∣<1/n on Kn−​,∣Pn​∣<1/n on Kn0​.
(12)
Every fixed point with ∣z∣<1 eventually belongs to the appropriate one of these three sets, according to the sign of its real part. These inequalities therefore give precisely the asserted pointwise limits.

3K (Coding & Cryptography)

Words: 210 Articles: 1
Paper 3 OurBigBook.com

Solution

Words: 210
3K OurBigBook.com
Let α be a primitive nth root of unity in an extension of Fq​, where gcd(n,q)=1. A BCH code of length n, initial exponent b, and design distance δ is the cyclic code whose generator polynomial is the least common multiple over Fq​ of the minimal polynomials of
αb,αb+1,…,αb+δ−2.
(13)
Thus every codeword polynomial c(X) vanishes at these δ−1 consecutive powers.
Suppose a nonzero codeword has weight w<δ, with
c(X)=∑ℓ=1w​cℓ​Xiℓ​,
(14)
where the positions iℓ​ are distinct modulo n and every cℓ​ is nonzero. The first w root conditions give
∑ℓ=1w​cℓ​αiℓ​(b+j)=0,j=0,1,…,w−1.
(15)
The coefficient matrix is a Vandermonde matrix in the distinct elements αi1​,…,αiw​, followed by multiplication of its columns by the nonzero factors αbiℓ​. Its determinant is therefore
(∏ℓ=1w​αbiℓ​)∏r<s​(αis​−αir​)=0.
(16)
Hence all cℓ​ would be zero, a contradiction. The minimum distance consequently satisfies d≥δ.
A code of minimum distance d detects every pattern of at most d−1 errors and uniquely corrects every pattern of at most ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors, because Hamming balls of that radius are disjoint. A BCH code of design distance δ is therefore guaranteed to detect δ−1 errors and to correct
⌊2δ−1​⌋
(17)
errors; its actual capabilities may be larger if d>δ.
Solved by gpt-5.6-sol high.

The instruction −(0,p,q) goes to p if register 0 is empty; otherwise it deletes the final letter and goes to q.
For M, an empty input goes directly from qS​ to q1​, where a 1 is appended. On a nonempty input, state q0​ deletes every letter; once the register is empty it goes to q2​ and appends 0. Hence
A={ε}.
(18)
For N, the initial instruction tests whether the final letter is 0. If it is, state q3​ deletes the entire word and then goes to q1​, producing 1. Otherwise state q0​ deletes the entire word and goes to q2​, producing 0. Thus
B={w0:w∈B},
(19)
the set of nonempty binary words ending in 0.

Rename the old halt state qH​ as a nonhalting state qF​, including every occurrence of qH​ in the original program, and introduce a new halt state qH​. Attach the following output-flipping routine:
qF​q0​q1​q+1​q+0​qH​​↦?0​(0,q0​,q1​)↦−(0,q+1​,q+1​)↦−(0,q+0​,q+0​)↦+1​(0,qH​)↦+0​(0,qH​)↦?ε​(0,qH​,qH​).​
(21)
Because the original machine computes a characteristic function, it reaches qF​ with register 0 containing exactly 0 or 1. The routine tests that symbol, removes it, and appends its complement. It therefore halts with 1−χX​(w)=χB∖X​(w).

Let Y1​,…,Yn​ be independent. In the general exponential-dispersion formulation, with known weights wi​>0 and common dispersion ϕ>0, their densities have the form
fi​(yi​;θi​,ϕ)=exp{ϕwi​​[yi​θi​−b(θi​)]+c(yi​,wi​ϕ​)}.
(22)
Thus
μi​=EYi​=b′(θi​),Var(Yi​)=wi​ϕ​b′′(θi​)=wi​ϕ​V(μi​).
(23)
The systematic component is ηi​=xiT​β, and a specified one-to-one differentiable link relates it to the mean by
g(μi​)=ηi​.
(24)
The unknown model parameters are the regression coefficient β and, when it is not fixed by the family, the dispersion ϕ.
The log-likelihood is
ℓ(β,ϕ)=∑i=1n​{ϕwi​​[yi​θi​−b(θi​)]+c(yi​,wi​ϕ​)},
(25)
up to terms independent of the parameters, where θi​ is determined from g−1(xiT​β)=b′(θi​).
For a Poisson response,
f(y;μ)=exp{ylogμ−μ−log(y!)},
(26)
so the natural parameter is θ=logμ and b(θ)=eθ. The canonical link sets the linear predictor equal to the natural parameter and is therefore
g(μ)=logμ​.
(27)

c OurBigBook.com
Fix the two conserved momenta pψ​=λ and pϕ​=μ. The remaining canonical variables (θ,pθ​) form a two-dimensional phase space with Hamiltonian
Hλ,μ​(θ,pθ​)=2Ipθ2​​+Vλ,μ​(θ),
(44)
where
Vλ,μ​(θ)=2Isin2θ(μ−λcosθ)2​+2Jλ2​+Mgacosθ.
(45)
An upright spinning solution has θ=0, pθ​=0, and necessarily μ=λ, since the vertical and body-axis angular momenta then coincide. On that momentum level,
Vλ,λ​(θ)=2Iλ2​tan22θ​+2Jλ2​+Mgacosθ.
(46)
Near zero,
Vλ,λ​(θ)=constant+(8Iλ2​−2Mga​)θ2+O(θ4).
(47)
Thus the upright configuration is a strict local minimum of the reduced Hamiltonian, and hence stable, when
λ2>4IMga=3IMgl​.
(48)
Here λ is the angular momentum about the symmetry axis. This proves stability for sufficiently large axial angular momentum.

A graph is eulerian graph if it has a closed trail containing every edge exactly once. For a graph with at least three vertices, the Euler circuit criterion says that it is Eulerian exactly when it is connected and every vertex has even degree.
Necessity is immediate: each visit of a closed trail to a vertex uses one entering and one leaving edge, so the incident edges occur in pairs; the trail also joins every vertex incident with an edge. Conversely, start at any vertex and extend an edge-simple trail until no unused incident edge remains. Even degrees force this maximal trail to end where it began. If edges remain, connectedness supplies a vertex of this circuit incident with an unused edge. Construct another closed trail from there and splice it into the first. Repeating consumes every edge and gives an Euler circuit.
The line graph L(G) has vertex set E(G), with two vertices adjacent when the corresponding edges of G share an endpoint. If G is connected and r-regular, then L(G) is connected, and the vertex corresponding to an edge uv has degree
(d(u)−1)+(d(v)−1)=2r−2.
(136)
Every degree is even, so the Euler circuit criterion makes L(G) Eulerian.

The Arzela-Ascoli theorem in sequential form states: if K is a compact metric space and (fn​) is a uniformly bounded, equicontinuous sequence in C(K), then it has a uniformly convergent subsequence. Equivalently, a subset of C(K) is relatively compact in the uniform norm exactly when it is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous.
For sufficiency, choose a finite 1/m-net Em​⊂K for every m. The union D=⋃m​Em​ is countable and dense. Uniform boundedness makes each scalar sequence (fn​(x))n​, x∈D, bounded. Successive applications of Bolzano-Weierstrass followed by a diagonal choice give a subsequence (gn​) for which gn​(x) converges at every x∈D.
Given ε>0, equicontinuity supplies δ>0 such that
d(x,y)<δ⟹∣gn​(x)−gn​(y)∣<ε/3
(177)
for every n. Choose a finite δ-net from D. Pointwise convergence on those finitely many points makes (gn​) uniformly Cauchy on the net, and the two equicontinuity estimates make it uniformly Cauchy on all of K. Since C(K) is complete, gn​ converges uniformly.
Conversely, a relatively compact family is uniformly bounded because its closure is compact in the normed space C(K). Given ε>0, cover that compact closure by finitely many uniform balls of radius ε/3, centred at continuous functions h1​,…,hr​. Uniform continuity of the finitely many hi​ gives one δ that works for all of them. Approximating any family member by one hi​ proves equicontinuity.

∑r,j​arj​um+jn+r​=0.
(471)
A spatial Fourier mode has the form
umn​=u,neimθ.
(472)
If one time step multiplies its amplitude by G, then u,n+r=Gru,n, and substitution gives the amplification polynomial of a multilevel finite difference scheme
r,j∑​arj​Greijθ=0​.
(473)
For a one-step method this equation directly determines
G(θ)=u,nu,n+1​.
(474)
By Parseval's identity, Von Neumann stability analysis gives 2-norm stability when ∣G(θ)∣≤1 for every Fourier mode. For a multilevel method, every root must obey the corresponding root condition.

∣qj​∣≤1
(489)

stability for every μ>0​.
